A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAMEN research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections A–D are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAMEN evaluations on eight PANGAEA segmentation tasks, component ablations, computational measurements, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds resampling-control results in Appendix Table C and further qualitative examples in Figure C.

M1.justification: The channel-conditioned projector, spatial resampler, temporal attention, shared transformer, and masked reconstruction objective are unchanged. The added experiments reuse resampling variants already defined in Section 4.4.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three pretraining datasets and eight PANGAEA tasks. The new ablations concern already-evaluated HLS BurnScars and Pastis; Figure C retains the same four datasets and resolution scenarios.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator sets are unchanged. New Appendix Table C reuses the same naive, false-encoding, and adjustable-resampling variants compared in Table 4b, extending their evaluation without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: The added controlled ablations evaluate validation mIoU at HLS BurnScars target GSDs of 1920, 960, 480, and 300 m and Pastis (S2) GSDs of 80, 40, and 20 m. These extend the resampling-ablation settings; the existing benchmark splits, training budgets, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 and new Table C extend the resampling ablation from Sen1Floods11 to HLS BurnScars and Pastis. Figure C adds three qualitative cases per dataset while retaining the original cases, broadening existing analyses of resolution-dependent predictions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports performance uncertainty through repeated training runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added 0.48 mIoU summary describes gains across evaluated conditions, not a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table C adds naive and false-encoding scores, such as 86.51 and 87.64 validation mIoU for BurnScars at 300 m, alongside the previously reported adjustable score of 88.44. It also supports a new 0.48 mIoU aggregate-gain statement. Additional qualitative predictions appear in Figure C; existing numerical results, including Table 1's 60.03 average mIoU, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations in Equations 1–7 and Appendix Equations A–B are unchanged. No theorem, proof, assumption, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about sensor-agnostic representations, controllable output resolution, and benchmark performance. The supplementary additions provide evidence for existing contributions.

C2.justification: The interpretations of scale-conditioned refinement, expert specialization, temporal fusion, and computational trade-offs remain unchanged. The new Appendix B.2 paragraph reiterates the existing resampling interpretation; it introduces no new mechanism explanation or applicability limitation.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, optimizer settings, hardware, training time, preprocessing, and evaluation implementation details are retained. The code and pretrained-model access statement is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 48 works and retain the same related-work discussion and novelty positioning. Changed citation back-reference pages reflect pagination only.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short paragraph in Appendix B.2, revises Figure C's caption, and updates table cross-references. The main narrative and section ordering are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Appendix Table C and renumbers the subsequent tables. Figure C changes from a combined four-dataset grid to four dataset-specific panels, each showing four examples. Other figures and table designs remain intact, with limited accompanying text reflow.

improvement.justification: New Table C strengthens evidence for the resampler's benefit beyond the original Sen1Floods11 ablation, while expanded Figure C makes prediction behavior across more scenes inspectable. These focused additions improve empirical support without changing the method, main benchmark results, or core claims.
